lines = open(sys.argv[1]).read().split("\n")
samples = []
cur = None
for l in lines:
    if l.startswith("== "):
        _, t, kids = l.split()
        cur = [int(t), int(kids), []]
        samples.append(cur)
    elif l and cur is not None:
        name = re.sub(r"\$40std\$2F[a-z-]+\$2Fsrc\$2F", "", l)
        name = name.replace("$2E", ".").replace("$2F", "/")
        name = re.sub(r"\$24.*", "", name)
        cur[2].append(name)
# the phase a stack is in: the deepest frame that names one
marks = [
    ("learned/answers taken", ["learned_taken", "core_taken", "wave_taken", "took_lent"]),
    ("waves forked/waited", ["waited_for", "forked_for", "asked_across_while", "turns_across"]),
    ("item_starts", ["item_starts"]),
    ("file_refused", ["file_refused"]),
    ("program_refused", ["program_refused"]),
    ("keys", ["keyed_objects", "frames_keyed"]),
    ("code hashes", ["program_code_hashes"]),
    ("walk", ["walked_from", "item_program.av.walked"]),
    ("program_walked", ["program_walked"]),
    ("program_reached", ["program_reached"]),
    ("store save", ["saved", "DiskStore"]),
    ("link", ["layered_refused", "link_refused", "clang_refused"]),
    ("start-up / frontier", ["frontier_open", "store_opened", "opened_store"]),
]
counts = collections.Counter()
for t, kids, frames in samples:
    phase = "other"
    for label, keys in marks:
        if any(any(k in f for k in keys) for f in frames):

    if serial and phase == "other":

for (serial, phase), n in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
    print("serial" if serial else "parallel", phase, n)

#!/bin/sh
# the parent's stack every 0.3 s across a cold cli build, with the tree's CPU at each sample
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
cd /work/avra
B=${SERIAL_BIN:-build/avra-try}
out=/work/probes/serial
mkdir -p $out
find $out -type f -delete
find packages/cli/.avra-cache .avra-cache /root/.avra/cache -delete 2>/dev/null
start=$(date +%s%N)
$B build packages/cli > $out/build.out 2>&1 &
bp=$!
while kill -0 $bp 2>/dev/null; do
  sleep 0.3
  kids=$(cat /proc/$bp/task/*/children 2>/dev/null | wc -w)
  t=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - start) / 1000000 ))
  echo "== $t $kids" >> $out/stacks
  gdb -q -batch -p $bp -ex 'thread 1' -ex 'bt 60' 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'in av_\S+' | sed 's/in av_//; s/(.*//' >> $out/stacks
done
wait $bp
echo "SERIAL DONE $(( ($(date +%s%N) - start) / 1000000 ))" > $out/done

<to_controller>#9 PARALLEL SERIAL MIDDLE, measurement (cold cli, c. aaa83b6f + chunks/frames, net off, 4 cores): 64.3 s wall.
Timeline (wall, CPU sampled every 0.5 s, stacks every 2 s, AVRA_QUERY_TIMES):
- 0–42 s: 6 work-ahead waves at ~3.4 cores. Serial INSIDE: each wave's parent start-up 0/0/0.2/0.7/0.9/1.5 s and answers taken 0/0/0/0.1/0.4/0.9 s, ≈4.7 s. Plus the generators wave's lock imbalance (cores waited 1.7–3.5 s on file_declares/file_generated).
- 42.5–46.0 s SERIAL (3.5 s): learned_taken/core_taken ~0.9 s, then program_walked → the walk (2.7 s whole, decoding UnitFacts.tests_in per unit).
- 46.0–49.5 s: parallel placement wave (program_placed across cores).
- 49.5–54.5 s SERIAL (5.0 s): wave_taken ~0.4 s, program_reached 1.4 s, program_refused 1.1 s (742 file_refused folds), keys 0.7 s (item_starts 0.4 of it), shape/hashes/seen ~1.4 s.
- 54.5–62.5 s: emit wave, 8.6 s at ~3.5 cores. LLVM codegen is only 10.9 CPU-s of ~30; the rest is per-chunk Avra work in the workers (bucket_asked, memory pass, IR build). Heaviest module 0.43 s (44k instrs), so no tail.
- 62.5–64.3 s SERIAL (1.8 s): world .so link 0.6 s + store save.
Total serial ≈ 15 s of 64.

Design (deterministic: per-file results are content-addressed answers; every merge sorts by symbol or file path):
1. Walk: each lowering core also writes per-file reach facts (callee symbol ids, declared BodySeen, sees inputs) as one answer per file. The parent's walk becomes a BFS over the merged, symbol-sorted adjacency, decoding no UnitFacts. 3.4 → ~0.6 s.
2. program_refused and keys: file_refused, unit_key_words and item_starts are per-file folds, run inside the placement wave; the parent concatenates in file order. 1.8 → ~0.2 s.
3. program_reached/shape/seen: built from the same per-file facts (files, unit_files, declared slices), merged by symbol sort. 2.8 → ~0.8 s.
4. Answers taken: each core publishes its answers as its own pack; the parent adopts the packs' sorted indexes (k-way merge by question hash) instead of re-taking each answer. ~2.6 s across waves → ~0.5 s.
5. Wave seams: fork the next wave from a parent whose frontier is already open, and put the store save behind the emit wave. ~3 s → ~1 s.
Claimed: serial 15 → ~4.5 s, cold wall 64 → ~54 s.
Receipts would be: two cold runs give byte-identical binaries and identical store answers; the timeline re-measured; the walk-order witness.
Which first? I'd start with 1+2+3 (one change: per-file reach facts), then 4.</to_controller>

I've measured the cold cli build and posted the measurement and design for #9; nothing is built yet.

**Measurement:** the cold `packages/cli` build takes 64.3 s on 4 cores with the net off. About 15 s of that runs on one core between the parallel waves:

| when | wall | what |
|---|---|---|
| inside the 0–42 s parallel waves | ≈4.7 s | each wave's start-up in the parent, and the parent taking the workers' answers |
| 42.5–46.0 s | 3.5 s | taking the workers' answers (~0.9 s), then the walk (2.7 s) |
| 49.5–54.5 s | 5.0 s | `program_reached` 1.4 s, `program_refused` 1.1 s, keys 0.7 s, shape and hashes ~1.4 s |
| 62.5–64.3 s | 1.8 s | linking the world `.so` (0.6 s) and saving the store |

- **Generators wave:** inside the waves, the cores also lose 1.7–3.5 s each waiting on locks (`file_declares` / `file_generated`).
- **Emit wave (8.6 s):** it has no heavy tail; the largest module is 0.43 s. LLVM codegen is only 10.9 of ~30 CPU-seconds; the rest is our own per-chunk work in the workers.

**Design proposal:**
- **Per-file facts:** each worker writes its files' reach facts, refusals and keys during the waves. The parent then only walks a merged graph sorted by symbol and concatenates results in file order.
- **Workers' answers:** each worker publishes its own store pack, and the parent merges their sorted indexes instead of taking every answer one at a time.
- **Wave seams:** the next wave forks from a parent whose store is already open, and the store save moves behind the emit wave.
- **Determinism:** every merge sorts by symbol or file path, so two runs should give byte-identical binaries and store answers.

I estimate serial time drops from about 15 s to 4.5 s, and the cold build from about 64 s to 54 s. My copy of `PROGRAM_DESIGN.md` is dated Nov 13 and has no "ARCHITECTURE FOR BOTH" section, so I worked from your brief rather than the roadmap text.

**Decision for you:** which part to start with. I'd do the per-file reach facts first, since one change covers the walk, refusals, keys and shape, then the pack merge.

I've measured the cold cli build and posted the measurement and design for #9; nothing is built yet.

**Measurement:** the cold `packages/cli` build takes 64.3 s on 4 cores with the net off. About 15 s of that runs on one core between the parallel waves:

| when | wall | what |
|---|---|---|
| inside the 0–42 s parallel waves | ≈4.7 s | each wave's start-up in the parent, and the parent taking the workers' answers |
| 42.5–46.0 s | 3.5 s | taking the workers' answers (~0.9 s), then the walk (2.7 s) |
| 49.5–54.5 s | 5.0 s | `program_reached` 1.4 s, `program_refused` 1.1 s, keys 0.7 s, shape and hashes ~1.4 s |
| 62.5–64.3 s | 1.8 s | linking the world `.so` (0.6 s) and saving the store |

- **Generators wave:** inside the waves, the cores also lose 1.7–3.5 s each waiting on locks (`file_declares` / `file_generated`).
- **Emit wave (8.6 s):** it has no heavy tail; the largest module is 0.43 s. LLVM codegen is only 10.9 of ~30 CPU-seconds; the rest is our own per-chunk work in the workers.

**Design proposal:**
- **Per-file facts:** each worker writes its files' reach facts, refusals and keys during the waves. The parent then only walks a merged graph sorted by symbol and concatenates results in file order.
- **Workers' answers:** each worker publishes its own store pack, and the parent merges their sorted indexes instead of taking every answer one at a time.
- **Wave seams:** the next wave forks from a parent whose store is already open, and the store save moves behind the emit wave.
- **Determinism:** every merge sorts by symbol or file path, so two runs should give byte-identical binaries and store answers.

I estimate serial time drops from about 15 s to 4.5 s, and the cold build from about 64 s to 54 s. My copy of `PROGRAM_DESIGN.md` is dated Nov 13 and has no "ARCHITECTURE FOR BOTH" section, so I worked from your brief rather than the roadmap text.

**Decision for you:** which part to start with. I'd do the per-file reach facts first, since one change covers the walk, refusals, keys and shape, then the pack merge.

#!/bin/sh
# a cold cli build's wall timeline: every half second, the CPU the build's process tree used since the
# last sample (in cores), how many processes it has, and every 2 s the main process's stack
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_EMIT_TIMES=1 AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1
cd /work/avra
B=${TL_BIN:-build/avra-try}
out=/work/probes/timeline
mkdir -p $out
find $out -type f -delete
find packages/cli/.avra-cache .avra-cache /root/.avra/cache -delete 2>/dev/null
hz=$(getconf CLK_TCK)
tree() { # the pids under $1, itself included
  echo $1
  for c in $(cat /proc/$1/task/*/children 2>/dev/null); do tree $c; done
}
ticks() { # utime+stime+cutime+cstime of every pid under $1
  s=0
  for p in $(tree $1); do
    t=$(awk '{print $14+$15+$16+$17}' /proc/$p/stat 2>/dev/null)
    s=$((s + ${t:-0}))
  done
  echo $s
}
start=$(date +%s%N)
$B build --time packages/cli > $out/build.out 2>&1 &
bp=$!
last=0; lastt=$start; n=0
while kill -0 $bp 2>/dev/null; do
  sleep 0.5
  now=$(date +%s%N)
  tk=$(ticks $bp)
  procs=$(tree $bp | wc -l)
  cores=$(awk -v a=$tk -v b=$last -v hz=$hz -v dt=$((now - lastt)) 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", (a - b) / hz / (dt / 1e9) }')
  echo "$(( (now - start) / 1000000 )) $cores $procs" >> $out/cpu
  last=$tk; lastt=$now
  n=$((n + 1))
  if [ $((n % 4)) = 0 ]; then
    echo "== $(( (now - start) / 1000000 ))" >> $out/stacks
    gdb -q -batch -p $bp -ex 'thread 1' -ex 'bt 40' 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'in av_\S+' | sed 's/in av_//; s/(.*//' | head -40 >> $out/stacks
  fi
done
wait $bp
echo "BUILD EXIT $? $(( ($(date +%s%N) - start) / 1000000 ))ms" >> $out/cpu
echo "TL DONE" > $out/done

169:- **Answers stream (2026-11-09, e6ca3edd).** Each answer is appended to a per-process draft (`@std/io` `Draft`: a temp named by pid and serial, published under a name chosen at the end) in 1 MiB writes, and read back through a mapping of the draft, remapped every 16 MiB. The process holds where answers lie, never their bytes. Publish appends the sorted index (`PackIndex`: answer spans and question records) and the seal; the pack is never built in memory. A failed write spoils the draft, so no index points at missing octets. Drafts of dead processes are swept when a store opens. Seal `avrapak3`.
952:Owners: lane C — 1, 8, then `it.params` and 2, 4, the three bodies of 3. Lane A — the `build` switch, then 7 (it is stage (b) `test`). Lane B — test side, then the walk half of 3 (inline lambda seats, `@stage`). Queued: 6 when `check` moves, 5 + 11 when the IR is next touched, 9, 10, 12, 13 opportunistic.
982:- Still owed: argument re-encoding per ask (octets + blake3) — a question memo keyed by the arguments' own values; causes 4 and 5. Target: the walk under 60 s cold.
987:- Re-measured, every `.avra-cache` in the worktree moved aside before EACH run, both binaries built the same way: `--built` cold 84.2 → 78.6 s (walk 78 → 74 s); `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 build packages/cli` cold 112.5 → 110.1 s; peak ~2.7 GB. Batch 1 is ~7% on the walk, ~2% on the build. Decode-once helps repeated reads, which a cold run barely has. The memo-on/off byte-identity still holds.
1003:- WALL TIME ON THIS MAC IS POLLUTED BY THE MEMORY POOL WAIT whenever another lane builds; compare CPU, or measure with the other lanes idle. Cold CPU: new 186 s (single-threaded) vs old 255 s (parallel workers).
1028:- No-op remaining (CPU): program made 6.7 s, bitcode for 31 modules ~3 s, startup ~1 s. Possible structural step: a saved query answering the bucket keys so a no-op skips the walk; trade to be brought to the lead first.
1128:- DEFECT FOUND BY LANE D, TOP CORRECTNESS ITEM: answers on the generator/scope chain depend on ASK ORDER — `file_scope → generated_names → file_generated → generator_print → lowered_under → impls_with → package_impls → resolved → file_scope`. In a different first-ask order it either closes into a cycle refusal or `file_generated` answers NO ITEMS (seen as a worker trap "index k out of bounds (length 0)"; 2 of 9 runs; a pinned hash seed does not determine it). Masked whenever answers are reused in the walk's order; exposed by any process whose first ask is a body in such a file (a warm edit, `check` of one file). Not the store, not the held memos. 194:  - **Deep nesting crashes.** 6,000 nested parentheses segfault `check` in a pass both parsers share, and `avra parsers` at 2,000. A runaway compiler recursion wants a trap with words, as a program's does at 100,000 calls.
199:  - **Old workspace.** A `src` directory named `weird.av` traps it, which predates both tracks.
219:- Defect, found by the first full std-avrac suite on a runner (run 42757152485, 14 GB ceiling: the suite's test binary peaks at 9.0 GB): 226 rule examples proved, the program proofs ran, and `features/collects/tests/closure_entry_b` evaluated to `[]` instead of `[knob]`. That test guards a batch: two programs sharing one store, one declaring a `@seat` in its entry file, must each read their own closure collect. Reproduced in miniature (a scratch package holding `closure_entry_a`, `closure_entry_b` and `closure_support` as nested tests, run by one `avra test`): `program`'s compiler fails it, **main's passes it** (main bootstrapped from main's seed). Each program alone passes. Not this session's typing or engine work (the old evaluation path uses neither); most likely the inherited 11-04/05 base-lane commits that made per-program answers lasting across a batch (`302c7eec` "the program's closure that fed them", `d263370e` Names lasting, `908d9341` a unit's lowering lasting). Diagnosed (no bisect possible: the lanes' trees each needed their day's compiler, none kept): the order matters one way — `b` after `a` reads `[]`, `b` first and both pass. `AVRA_QTRACE` shows `b` taking 149 lowered units straight from the store: `lowered_unit_of` is a lasting answer keyed by its want (d0e27583), and a unit's reads are its syntax plus what it asks. A `closure` collect's members (`gathered_by_mark`/`gathered_into`, features/decls.av) depend on the program being built but are no recorded read, so `owners()`'s unit, with the collect baked empty by `a`, stands for `b`. A silent wrong-output defect for any two programs sharing a cache. Fix, and why a recorded read is not one: the unit's key carries no program, so any read `a` recorded keeps verifying in `b`'s process (`a`'s closure didn't move). A closure collect's members belong to the final program, as a linker's registration table does (C++ static registration, Rust's `inventory`). So the library's unit must not bake them: lower a closure collect's members as a static unit keyed by the program being built, referenced from the library's unit by symbol. Library units stay shared across programs; only the program's own small unit holds the table. The program layer's lowering takes the same shape from the start. **Fixed in the old compiler (65c7e283):** a closure-scoped collect's own unit is `unkept` (as a unit with voices already is), so it's lowered for each program and never served to another; every other unit stays shared. Witnessed by the miniature batch in both orders, eval == native == expected (a then b failed before). The full suite is rerunning on the runner to confirm.
228:- Machine safety: BUILT (0d5a5083). Past a 256 MB allowance every Avra process reserves its memory from a machine-wide pool (60% of RAM, 256 MB slots, an flock per slot the kernel drops on exit); a run holding nothing waits, one holding slots waits 120 s then refuses in its own words; `make pool-check` holds it with real processes. Agents can run in parallel again under it.
347:  - Found: kinds named by bare name collide. `Variant` is both a node and a helper type, so one kind has two shapes. The schema names kinds by their whole path.
397:- **A meaning stands where its instance does.** A declaration owns its nodes by allocation order ("source order is ownership order"), so an instance's meaning is allocated at the instance, before the statements around it. Expanding at the end of a parse, or even at the end of its item, puts meanings outside their declaration's run and the memory pass reads out of bounds (both were tried). So a parse that has the component expands inline, as it always did, and a parse that reads only a word's shape (`Instancing.Shaped`) leaves the instance meaning nothing; reading a tape back reads each instance's expansion at the instance, so the allocation order is a parse's.
438:  - The tape schema is a const read off the declarations (`Reading.tapes_schema`); no derive generates schema, and `[lifted]` is gone from both manifests.
475:- **Merged.** `program-scope` (track B) merged at c70ae14a/2204478f. `program-parser` (track C): its ten commits landed in `program` one at a time as reviewed cherry-picks, and e8717b05 records the merge (`git cherry` marks all ten patch-equivalent; the trees differ only by `program`'s later `pool-check`). Both branches are ancestors of `program`.
482:    - a module that is both a file and a directory losing its files;
486:  - Decided for the program layer, against the old workspace: a third file's read of a name two siblings keep private stays `KeptApart` even when the prelude exports it (CLAUDE.md's law; the workspace lends the prelude's), and a name declared as both a fn and a type binds both spaces (the workspace binds the type, then refuses the call).
569:    - A reviewing agent's probes found two defects in the first draft, both fixed with witnesses: (1) an unhashed query's code can change under one print, so the frontier served its readers' old answers; now such a query is read afresh like an input. (2) a save that compacted before the frontier was written left a frontier naming dropped answers, and the next process trapped; now the store holds the frontier as pending, seeds compaction from it, and writes the file only after the pack holding its answers is published.
597:8. **Parallel by declaration**: bodies are independent, so typing fans out across cores like the cold parse.
613:Order: the memory pool (a machine-wide memory reservation every heavy process takes before starting, so parallel tracks can't crash the machine); the typing core (2, 3, 4, 5) with the If/literal/call/let slice as code; the `check` component (1), proven by porting that slice; the rest of the features in parallel tracks; then 7 and 8.
617:**The observation everything follows from.** A feature's meaning and a `@derive` are the same thing: code that writes code. `x ?? d` means `match x { v? -> v, null -> d }`; `@derive(Saved)` means "these methods, written so". Today the two live in different worlds: 4,700 lines of per-feature lowering emit IR by hand, and generators run in a separate expansion engine. Collapse them (P6). **Every feature means a rewrite into a small core of Avra, written as a quote, and a generator is the same kind of rewrite.** One engine elaborates both; only the core reaches the machine.
636:**7. Two engines, one IR, and a fast dev path.** The interpreter runs generators and `avra run` straight off the IR, with no LLVM. Release builds emit LLVM per unit, in parallel across cores, each object cached by IR hash, so a one-fn edit compiles one fn.
646:**Approved by the owner 2026-11-10, with all five additions:** (1) typed holes `${x: Type}`; (2) a quote-to-quote arm read backwards: resugaring in errors and `explain`, code actions both ways; (3) `@example(before, after)` on any arms component, generalising `rule`'s `@fixes`/`@keeps`, run by the compiler and shown in docs; (4) every instance's arms compiled into one matcher, refusing an arm that can never fire and a sugar kind with no meaning; (5) template names fresh, a name for the user's code spelled `${name("it")}`.
648:**Spelling:** no new syntax. `meaning` is an ordinary component, `export component meaning { run: fn(dyn Subject) -> Code? }`, written the way `rule` already is: an arms body, quote patterns on the left, quotes on the right — `meaning coalesce { quote { ${left} ?? ${right} } -> quote { match ${left} { v? -> v, null -> ${right} } } }`. Type-directed choice is an arm guard (`if xs.type()…`, as `str_grown_quadratically` already writes); a typed hole `${xs: List<_>}` is the sugar both `rule` and `meaning` want. The first draft's `meaning X { fields } = quote {…}` was new syntax and is dropped.
669:  - cli: 100 alike plus 4 answering their seat of 108, **0 differing**, 4 untyped on a side. Three of those are untyped on both sides; one is a `??` in a comprehension clause the core pass leaves untyped.
673:  - Receipt, 0 differing: std-text 11/11; cli 199 alike plus 5 answering their seat of 208; std-program 67 of 77, 10 untyped on both sides (derive code).
732:7. LLVM per unit, cached by hash, in parallel.
756:   - **LLVM stays** the native, optimising path, and parallelism and laws go through it as decided on 09-22. C is an additional target, never a detour.
781:5. **Parallelism and GPU from purity.** The `Reach` column already says what is pure. The lowering forks pure subtrees, such as a large `map`, where the target's cost model says it pays, on a work-stealing pool. A `target nvptx` is one more template file, through LLVM as decided on 09-22.
787:- **Two divergences cut and counted, both needing whole-program facts:** the cancel test after a call that may reach a cancel point, and the scheduler's tick.
802:- **C. The six ideas:** (1) proven rules, then (4) live programs, then (2) Futamura, (3) the learning superoptimiser, (5) parallelism and GPU, and (6) omniscient debugging.
824:- **Hard parts.** Identical error messages and recovery, because exact-output tests pin them. LLVM's compile time on large generated functions, unmeasured. The tree-walking engine stays for grammars assembled at runtime, so both must agree.
825:- **Proof.** Run both engines over the real tree and compare trees and errors; any difference is a named bug.
841:- **`tapes <dir> --ran`** (a program test built through the new path, run in the evaluator and natively, held to `.expected`): 370 program tests under `features/*/tests`, 122 made on the program layer, 122 printing their `.expected` in both engines, 0 failing.
873:- The old typer refuses `impl Tr<T> for X<T>` (the trait's argument being the impl's own parameter) on any generic type, and a record holding a `Task` is `type.task_escape`. Both block `Waitable<T>` only while the OLD typer checks `@std/task`.
987:- Re-measured, every `.avra-cache` in the worktree moved aside before EACH run, both binaries built the same way: `--built` cold 84.2 → 78.6 s (walk 78 → 74 s); `AVRA_PROGRAM=1 build packages/cli` cold 112.5 → 110.1 s; peak ~2.7 GB. Batch 1 is ~7% on the walk, ~2% on the build. Decode-once helps repeated reads, which a cold run barely has. The memo-on/off byte-identity still holds.
995:| old path cold | 188 s | 255 s (parallel object workers) | 3.5 GB | waited on the pool |

# Spans: frames per file (aaa83b6f)

## Design as built
- **Lowering:** a body's unwind frame (`frame$<sym>`, the `Loc` an unwind reports) counts its
  site from its item's start (the item store's own span) and names the item (`Static.at_item`) and
  its file (`Static.home`). Nothing in a lowered answer holds a file-absolute place any more: the
  instructions never did, and this frame was the only absolute place.
- **The one add:** `placed_frames` → `file_placed(engine, file, item, FindingAt)`, applied where a
  unit's lowered body is taken into a program (`shaped_taken`, `taken_walk`). Every whole-program
  path, the evaluator and compile-time runs included, sees placed frames.
- **Chunks:** a chunk's module declares its bodies' frames (`Static.elsewhere`) and never defines
  them, so no chunk object holds a place.
- **Frames modules:** `Owned.Frames(at)`, one per file the program reads. It defines no bodies, and
  lays out that file's frames, placed and shared (external linkage under the linker's escaped name,
  `avra_mangle_symbol`). Its key = salt + file + `item_starts(file)` (a new cut query, one read per
  file) + the file's units' keys. The shape records each unit's file (`files`, `unit_files`), so
  keys need no unit decoding.
- **Not covered:** `written_site`'s `pkg/path:LINE` task-site lines stay in lowering. An edit that
  adds a newline above a body that spawns a task still re-keys that body. The same per-file
  treatment can follow.

## Receipts
- **Emit on packages/cli (K=1024, net off; owed objects/fns emitted):**

  | edit | emit | objects owed |
  |---|---|---|
  | leaf, same length | 46 ms | 3 (the edited fn's chunk, last chunk, shared.av's frames) |
  | leaf, growing | **35–37 ms**, was 0.31–0.34 s | the same 3 |
  | core | 113–130 ms | 12 |

  Cold: 55 s total, emit 8.1 s, 1,765 objects (1,024 chunks + 741 frames modules). Warm wall for a
  growing edit: ~1.0 s.
- **`lower` row:** ~150 ms here for both this compiler and the pre-change one on the same tree
  (AVRA_QUERY_TIMES: "the keys" 0.1 s in each), so frames add nothing measurable there. The
  pre-change compiler re-lowers 47 units and emits in 332 ms on the same edit.
- **Byte identity** (growing edit, incremental vs from empty stores): release binary identical
  (`cmp`). Dev: all 1,765 objects identical by key, none missing.
- **Trap place:** tools/frame_place_attack.sh (witness-b). A `within` times out over `nap`, and the
  unwind's frame for `nap` must equal `nap`'s body place and line in the source as it now reads:
  cold; after `pad` lengthened on its line; after `pad` given two more lines; after `pad` put back.
  None of the edits may owe `nap`'s chunk.
  - This compiler: 4 held (`nap:82-111` line 5 → `87-116` line 5 → `109-138` line 8 → `82-111`).
  - Pre-change compiler: 2 FAILED (nap's chunk owed on both edits). The attack tells the two apart.
- **tools/chunk_owed_attack.sh pins:** now count each edited file's frames module, plus the frames of
  a file whose units re-keyed: 2/4/5/7/5.
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# A FRAME SAYS WHERE ITS BODY STANDS IN ITS FILE, HOWEVER THE ITEMS ABOVE IT MOVED, AND MOVING THEM
# REMAKES NO CHUNK OF THE BODY'S. A body's frame counts its place from its item's start, and its file's
# frames module places it once, at emit, so an edit above the body remakes that module and the edited
# body's chunk. Held to each step: the program prints where a `within`'s unwind says `nap` stands, which
# must be the place and the line of `nap`'s body in the source as it now reads, and an edit above `nap`
# — one that lengthens a line, one that adds lines — owes no chunk `nap` is home to.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"
who=frame-place-attack
. tools/lib/steps.sh
R=build/frame-place
avra=${FRAME_ATTACK_AVRA:-./avra}
find "$R" -delete 2>/dev/null

The bundle `/work/avra-lane-lowering-quality.bundle` covers base55..008b0d3e, and the notes are in `/work/avra-lane-lowering-quality.md`.

**#11 result on `packages/cli`** (net off, chunk count K=1024):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| warm edit, same length, cli file | 1.0 s | 41–49 ms |
| warm edit in core | 0.40 s | 0.10–0.12 s |
| warm edit that changes a line's length | ~1.0 s | 0.31–0.34 s |
| cold build | 57–61 s | 59 s (no change) |

- **What changed:** a function now lands in one of 1,024 chunks chosen by its own name, so adding or removing a function moves no other function. Each chunk is reused whenever the keys of what it holds are unchanged, and those keys include the signatures and record layouts of everything its functions call.
- **A per-module cost fix along the way:** every module was decoding the whole program's list of ~32k function signatures. That is now read once per build, and per-module cost dropped about 10x.
- **Why K=1024:** following your rule, it's the smallest chunk count that keeps warm emit at or under 0.15 s for both same-length cli edits and core edits, and its cold time is lowest among those. At 4096 chunks the cold link fails, so that's out. The full curve is in the notes.
- **Attacks:** a callee body edit, an answer-type change, an added default parameter, a record layout change, and a new function each make exactly the expected chunks rebuild, and every resulting binary prints the right output. `tools/chunk_owed_attack.sh` pins those counts and is now a row in the `witness-b` slice.
- **Byte-identity:** an incremental release build is byte-identical to a cold one, and all 1,024 dev objects match by key. Dev binaries themselves differ by design, because dev builds link in layers.

**Limits no chunk count fixes:**
- **Line-length edits:** the compiled code stores source positions as absolute byte offsets, so any edit that changes a line's length rebuilds every later function in that file (41 in the test edit). Making positions relative to their function would bring these edits down to the same-length cost; I've proposed that as the next item.
- **Code hashes:** a one-function edit changes 236 of the program's 238 code hashes, so their small bodies stay together in one chunk that rebuilds on every edit.

**Two other findings to know about:**
- **Stale standing compiler:** a compiler built once from the standing `build/avra` crashes every std-avrac test. That standing binary's code generator wrongly adds the NUL check to the inert `avra_sw_text` call. Building twice fixes it, which matches your note.
- **The net's cost:** with the net on (the default), a warm one-edit build takes 98 s; with it off, 2.3 s. As you said, removing it is the parity lanes' work.

The by-value fold changes one behaviour: a generic one-field record or all-unit enum applied to type arguments no longer counts as compared-by-value for component props or list-scan warnings. That now matches what `==` already enforces.

# By-value law folded (285dcfb4)
core/checking.av's `compares_by_value` is the one definition, over a `Shapes` reader (record, name,
enum). A checked program hands out its own (`CheckedProgram.shapes()`), and the engine's readers with
no body in hand build one from the declarations (`declared_shapes(engine)`). The engine's copy in
item_signatures.av is gone. Behaviour change: a generic one-field record or all-unit enum applied to
arguments is no longer by-value for a component prop's cell or a list scan's miss, which matches `==`.
Gate: avrac-a/g/b, findings-a, sound, fmt, idioms-avrac PASS.

# #11 per-fn object cache (008b0d3e)

## Design as built
- **Grain:** a body falls in chunk `fp(symbol) mod 1023` (`symbol_bucket`, one definition shared by
  key-making and emit's `program_bucket`). The last chunk (1023) holds the code-hash bodies. A unit's
  bodies and its lambdas are homed at its symbol. An added or removed body moves no other body's chunk.
- **Key:** a chunk's key = salt (compiler, backend code hash, opt, inline mode, target, linked
  archives) + its chunk index + each unit's key (its lowering answer hash, symbol, tests kept, and
  `sees`, the digest of the seats, answer and consumed marks of every body and row it names). No
  bitcode is written to make a key.
- **Where:** the program layer's own object dir (`.avra-cache/tapes-build/obj`, keyed paths). No
  second cache.
- **Link:** unchanged. Dev builds link layered (world `.so` plus an overlay of what moved); release
  builds link whole over the kept objects.
- **Per-module cost:** the shape's declared bodies and extern rows are read once per build
  (`seen_bodies`) before the forked workers. Each module looks up only the names its bodies name, for
  its declared stubs and for the consumed-mark stand-ins the memory pass reads. Before this, every
  module decoded the whole program's ~32k `BodySeen`; a gdb sample of the workers put that at ~60%
  of per-module time.

## Receipt 0: the curve (packages/cli, AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0, cold = both stores cleared)
| K | cold total | cold emit | leaf, same length | leaf, grows | core edit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (file buckets, 32) | 57.3 s | 6.30 s | 0.97–1.01 s (1,895 fns) | 0.94–1.02 s | 0.39–0.40 s |
| 128 | 61.3 s | 6.07 s | 0.15–0.26 s | 1.4–1.5 s | 1.6–1.7 s |
| 512 | 59.7 s | 6.53 s | 42–48 ms | 0.51–0.56 s | 158–194 ms |
| **1024 (chosen)** | **59.1 s** | 7.25 s | **41–49 ms** (2 mods, 267 fns) | 308–341 ms (41 mods) | **100–117 ms** (11 mods) |
| 2048 | 60.9 s | 7.93 s | 35–39 ms | 201–210 ms | 112–134 ms |
| 4096 | link fails | — | 33–37 ms | 165–615 ms | 81–113 ms |

(The K=128 row was measured before `seen_bodies` landed; its warm and cold-emit numbers carry the old
per-module cost.) Cold totals are within run-to-run noise (57–61 s); cold emit grows about 1 ms of
wall per extra module. K=1024 is the smallest K meeting warm emit ≤ 0.15 s for both same-length leaf
and core edits, and has the lowest cold total among those. At 4096 the cold link fails (the world
`.so` is never written; at 8192 too).

**What no K fixes:**
- **(a) Absolute spans.** The lowered IR carries byte offsets, so an edit that changes the length of
  any text re-keys every later fn in its file (shared.av: 41 units). Making spans relative to their fn
  would make a growing edit cost what a same-length one does. That is a separate item.
- **(b) Code hashes are transitive.** A one-fn edit moves 236 of the cli's 238 code hashes, so the hash
  bodies stay together in the last chunk (~238 tiny bodies, re-emitted every edit).
- **(c) Generic code.** A core edit owes 11 chunks because the edited generic code is instantiated 11
  times across the program.

## Receipts
- **Attacks** (two-file package, each from empty stores, each binary's output checked):

  | edit | chunks owed | home to |
  |---|---|---|
  | callee body | 1 | the callee |
  | callee answer retyped, caller unedited | 2 | the callee and `said` |
  | callee given a defaulted seat | 3 | the callee, its default, `twice` |
  | record laid out anew (field before `a`) | 5 | `make`, `get`, the field default, the 2 entry chunks |
  | fn added at a file's end, called from the entry | 3 | the new fn and the 2 entry chunks |

  In the fn-added case, no other unit's chunk moved. Adding the fn mid-file with a longer `use` line
  also re-owed `twice`, `plain` and `said` in their own unchanged chunks: that is the span effect (a),
  not membership.
- **Byte identity** (cli, cold, then one edit built incrementally, vs the edited tree from empty
  stores): release binary identical (`cmp`). Dev: all 1,024 objects identical by key, none missing.
- **Gate row:** tools/chunk_owed_attack.sh, in witness-b, holds the five counts and owed symbols above
  exactly.
EOF
echo ok

program layer: a program's objects are chunks by symbol, each owing only what moved

A body falls in the chunk of its symbol's hash (1024 chunks, the last the code
hashes'), so an edit remakes the chunks its moved bodies fall in and an added or
removed body moves no other's. A chunk's key is its bodies' keys, each holding
what it sees of the bodies it names, so a callee's seats, answer or a record's
layout moving remakes every caller's chunk. The bodies and rows the shape
declares are read once a build, before the modules are made, and each module
reads only the names its bodies name, so a module costs what it holds.

A traced build says the objects it owes (`Q objects`, each owed chunk and the
symbols it is home to); tools/chunk_owed_attack.sh holds each edit kind's count
to its pin in the gate's witness-b slice.

#!/bin/sh # AN EDIT OWES THE CHUNKS ITS MOVED BODIES FALL IN, AND NO OTHERS. A program's bodies fall in chunks by # their symbols' hashes, each chunk an object kept under the keys of what it holds, so one edit of each # kind, made to a built program, owes exactly the chunks pinned here — counted from the build's # `Q objects` line and named by the symbols each owed chunk is home to — and the binary prints what the # source says. # claims. The sourcing script names its voice in `who` first.
#
#   say <words>       a claim that held (counted in `steps`)
#   fail <words>      a claim that did not (counted in `fails`)

fail() { fails=$((fails + 1)); echo "$who: FAILED — $1"; }

    if [ "$fails" != 0 ]; then
        echo "$who: $fails FAILED, $steps held${1:+ — $1}"
        return 1
    fi
    if [ "$steps" = 0 ]; then echo "$who: held${1:+ — $1}"; else echo "$who: $steps held${1:+ — $1}"; fi
}

# THE FLOOR OF AN ATTACK, sourced after `set -u` (`. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"`): stands in the
# tree's root, runs under the lock its caller holds (no second watchdog) and takes no compile slot.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
export AVRA_WATCH_HELD=1
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
export AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=0
fails=0
steps=0

# Marks a fixture directory as a checkout whose store is its own, cold, never the tree's.
own_store() {
    : > "$1/.git"
    export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/$1/.avra-cache"
}

# One failed check, counted and named.
fail() {
    fails=$((fails + 1))
    echo "FAIL  $*"
}

# The attack's last line — what it ran, then how much failed — and its status.
verdict() {
    echo "$1: $2, $fails failed"
    [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]
}

#!/bin/sh
# A KEPT OBJECT IS ALWAYS DROPPABLE. A program's objects are kept in its package's
# `.avra-cache/tapes-build/obj`, each by its key; a build owes the ones it can't find there and
# makes them again. Held to each step: the build passes, its binary prints what the source says,
# and the objects it made are counted — an edit makes few, an edit after every object was deleted
# makes them all, and a build after that makes none. A build that changed nothing stands on its
# kept binary whatever was deleted beside it, and a deleted binary is put back.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"
who=obj-gone-attack
. tools/lib/steps.sh
R=build/obj-gone
find "$R" -delete 2>/dev/null
mkdir -p $R/app/src $R/lib/src
own_store $R
printf '[package]\nname = "@rt/oglib"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n\n[lib]\nname = "rt-oglib"\npath = "src/lib.av"\n' > $R/lib/avra.toml
printf '[package]\nname = "og"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n\n[dependencies]\n"@rt/oglib" = { path = "../lib" }\n' > $R/app/avra.toml
printf 'export fn one() -> int { 1 }\nexport fn two() -> int { one() + 1 }\n' > $R/lib/src/lib.av
O=$R/app/.avra-cache/tapes-build/obj
main() { printf 'use @rt.oglib.{two}\n\nprintln("%s ${two()}")\n' "$1" > $R/app/src/main.av; }
# build <label> <want> <made>: the build passes, prints <want>, and made <made> objects
# ("some": at least one, fewer than all; "all": every object it keeps)
build() {
    touch $R/mark
    ./avra build $R/app > $R/out 2> $R/err || { fail "$1: the build failed: $(grep -v '^Q' $R/err | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"; return; }
    got=$($R/app/src/main 2>&1)
    [ "$got" = "$2" ] || { fail "$1: printed '$got', the source says '$2'"; return; }
    made=$(find $O -type f -newer $R/mark | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    kept=$(find $O -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    case $3 in
        some) [ "$made" -gt 0 ] && [ "$made" -lt "$kept" ] || { fail "$1: made $made of $kept objects, where an edit makes some"; return; } ;;
        all) [ "$made" -gt 0 ] && [ "$made" = "$kept" ] || { fail "$1: made $made of $kept objects, where every one was deleted"; return; } ;;
        *) [ "$made" = "$3" ] || { fail "$1: made $made objects, wanted $3"; return; } ;;
    esac
    say "$1: made $made of $kept objects, printed '$got'"
}
main n; build "cold" "n 2" all
main m; build "main edited, the library's objects kept" "m 2" some
build "nothing changed" "m 2" 0
find $O -type f -delete
build "every object deleted, nothing changed: the kept binary stands" "m 2" 0
find $O -type f -delete; find $R/app/src/main -delete
build "every object and the binary deleted, nothing changed" "m 2" 0
find $O -type f -delete; main k
build "every object deleted, main edited: each made again" "k 2" all
build "again, nothing changed" "k 2" 0
main j; build "edited once more" "j 2" some
printf 'export fn one() -> int { 3 }\nexport fn two() -> int { one() + 1 }\n' > $R/lib/src/lib.av
build "the library edited" "j 4" some
verdict
slice_witness_b() {
    row runs-witness sh tools/witness_program_runs.sh build/avra
    row heir-save-attack env HEIR_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/heir_save_attack.sh
    row share-merge-attack env SHARE_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/share_merge_attack.sh
    row beside-attack env BESIDE_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/beside_attack.sh
    row wave-share-attack env WAVE_ATTACK_AVRA="$root/build/avra" sh tools/wave_share_attack.sh
    row flow-trace make -s -o avra flow-trace
    row compiler-key sh tools/witness_compiler_key.sh build/avra
    row docs-cache-attack sh tools/docs_cache_attack.sh
    row obj-gone-attack sh tools/obj_gone_attack.sh
    row moved-tree-attack sh tools/moved_tree_attack.sh
    row layer-sites-attack sh tools/layer_sites_attack.sh
    row closure-gather-attack sh tools/closure_gather_attack.sh
    row store-bound-attack sh tools/store_bound_attack.sh
    row path-leak-attack sh tools/path_leak_attack.sh
    row case-leftover-attack sh tools/case_leftover_attack.sh
    old_row fixes-witness sh tools/witness_program_fixes.sh build/avra
    row root-listing-attack sh tools/root_listing_attack.sh
    row two-compilers-attack sh tools/two_compilers_attack.sh
    old_row ledger-witness sh tools/witness_program_ledger.sh build/avra
    old_row suites-witness sh tools/witness_program_suites.sh build/avra
    old_row doors-witness sh tools/witness_program_doors.sh build/avra
    old_row differential-witness sh tools/witness_program_differential.sh build/avra
}

#!/bin/sh
# byte identity: the edited tree built incrementally vs built from empty stores
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
cd /work/avra
B=build/avra-try
LEAF=packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av
out=/work/probes/ident
mkdir -p $out
find $out -mindepth 1 -delete
cp $LEAF $out/leaf.orig
log=$out/log
clear() { find packages/cli/.avra-cache .avra-cache /root/.avra/cache -delete 2>/dev/null; }
edited() { python3 -I /work/probes/edit.py $LEAF $out/leaf.orig "· memo" "identity-edit"; }
for mode in dev release; do
  flag=""; [ $mode = release ] && flag="--release"
  clear
  cp $out/leaf.orig $LEAF
  $B build $flag packages/cli > $out/$mode-orig.out 2>&1; echo "$mode orig exit $?" >> $log
  edited
  $B build $flag packages/cli > $out/$mode-inc.out 2>&1; echo "$mode incremental exit $?" >> $log
  cp packages/cli/src/main $out/$mode-inc.bin
  mkdir -p $out/$mode-inc-obj && cp packages/cli/.avra-cache/tapes-build/obj/*.o $out/$mode-inc-obj/
  clear
  $B build $flag packages/cli > $out/$mode-cold.out 2>&1; echo "$mode cold exit $?" >> $log
  cp packages/cli/src/main $out/$mode-cold.bin
  mkdir -p $out/$mode-cold-obj && cp packages/cli/.avra-cache/tapes-build/obj/*.o $out/$mode-cold-obj/
  n=0; missing=0; differ=0
  for o in $out/$mode-cold-obj/*.o; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    i=$out/$mode-inc-obj/$(basename $o)
    if [ ! -f $i ]; then missing=$((missing + 1)); elif ! cmp -s $o $i; then differ=$((differ + 1)); fi
  done
  echo "$mode objects: $n made cold, $missing not in the incremental store, $differ differing bytes" >> $log
  if cmp -s $out/$mode-inc.bin $out/$mode-cold.bin; then echo "$mode binary: identical" >> $log; else echo "$mode binary: DIFFERS" >> $log; fi
  $out/$mode-cold.bin --help > /dev/null 2>&1; echo "$mode binary runs: exit $?" >> $log
done
cp $out/leaf.orig $LEAF
find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -delete 2>/dev/null
cmp -s $out/leaf.orig $LEAF && echo "restored" >> $log
echo "IDENT DONE" >> $log

#!/bin/sh
# poor man's profiler: sample the stacks of the build's forked emit workers
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CHUNKS=${K:-2048}
cd /work/avra
find packages/cli/.avra-cache .avra-cache /root/.avra/cache -delete 2>/dev/null
out=/work/probes/pmp
mkdir -p $out
find $out -type f -delete
build/avra-try build packages/cli > $out/build.out 2>&1 &
bp=$!
n=0
while kill -0 $bp 2>/dev/null; do
  kids=$(pgrep -P $bp | head -4)
  cnt=$(echo "$kids" | grep -c .)
  if [ "$cnt" -ge 2 ]; then
    for k in $kids; do
      gdb -q -batch -p $k -ex 'bt 25' > $out/s$n-$k.txt 2>/dev/null
      n=$((n + 1))
    done
  fi
  sleep 1
  [ $n -ge 120 ] && break
done
wait $bp
echo "PMP DONE $n" >> $out/done

row() { grep -o 'emit [0-9]*ms' "$1" | head -1; }

  export AVRA_CHUNKS=$k

  s=$(date +%s%N)

    echo "K=$k leaf$i exit $st ms $(ms $s) $(row $out/leaf-$k-$i.out) $(emitted $out/leaf-$k-$i.out)" >> $log

  cp $out/leaf.orig $LEAF

content.text:
<to_controller>#11 per-fn object cache, design (posting before building):
1. KEY, per fn: H(compiler_id, target, build mode/opt, runtime id, body.fingerprint_in(ids), the layout fingerprint of every type the body names, the declared signature (row/LLVM fn type) of every symbol it calls or addresses, the layout of every static it addresses). Computed from IR fingerprints, never by writing bitcode to key it. Today the 32 roaming buckets write bitcode every build just to get their keys; that's part of the 0.4 s of driver work.
2. GRAIN: today's object per file becomes chunks keyed by their members' fn keys. A fn goes to a chunk by a stable hash of its symbol, so membership is a pure function of the program. An edit re-codegens only the chunks holding a moved key. Chunk size comes from a measured per-LLVM-module fixed cost (receipt 0). Size 1 is strict per fn; I expect ~16–64 so the cold build (32.7k fns) doesn't pay that cost 32k times.
3. WHERE: the program store, `Stored.Obj` under `node_key(Stored.Obj, ["fn-chunk", …])`. No second cache; misses use the existing objects_kept / keep_file path.
4. LINK: stays one full deterministic link over store paths (0.14 s measured, not the cost). It is incremental in its inputs: unchanged chunks are standing store objects, with no `ld -r` stage and no incremental linker, so byte-identity holds.
5. RECEIPTS: (0) per-module fixed cost, which sets the chunk size; (a) one-edit warm build before/after, net off, emit row and `Q objects` owed/total; (b) cold-then-warm vs cache-disabled builds of the same tree give byte-identical binaries (cmp); (c) attack: change a callee's signature, then a record's layout, without touching callers in other files. Every caller's chunk must miss and the binary must run right. Control: a body-only callee edit misses only the callee's chunk.
6. Then gate slices as usual.
Separately: fold done, 285dcfb4 (core's law over a `Shapes` reader; engine copy deleted). Behaviour change: a generic one-field record or all-unit enum applied to arguments no longer counts as by-value for component props or list-scan misses, matching `==`. Gate on it running next.
Go on 1–5, or a ruling on chunk vs strict per-fn first?</to_controller>

# Dev-backend note (#12): what a dev build's emit costs, and what a direct emitter would buy

All numbers: tree `c68ab5d0`, gen-2 `build/avra`, 4 cores, `AVRA_EMIT_TIMES=1`, dev (non-release)
`build/avra build packages/cli --time`. "built" = our IR -> LLVM IR on the program thread; "codegen" =
LLVM -O0 codegen + object into memory (the optimizer is skipped at level 0).

## 1. Cold (both stores cleared): emit is under 5% of the build
- Wall 152 s, user 269 s CPU, sys 19 s, peak RSS 4.2 GB (`/usr/bin/time -v`; a second run gave 151 s).
- 32 modules, 32,718 fns, 1,690,842 IR instructions emitted.
- Our IR -> LLVM IR: **2.3 s CPU**. LLVM codegen: **8.8 s CPU**. First hand-off to last object: 10.1 s
  summed over modules. `--time` line: analyze 1.5 s, lower 0.16 s, emit 6.2 s wall, link 0.33 s.
- About 140 s of the cold wall is query and analysis work that the `--time` rows don't name.
  A dev emitter can't touch it.

## 2. Warm one-edit loop: THE NET dominates; with it off, emit is the largest part
Same leaf edit (a comment in `cli/src/commands/shared.av`), `build/avra build --time packages/cli`:

| net | wall | analyze | lower | emit | link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| on (shipped default) | **98.0 s** (3 runs: 97.4 / 95.6 / 96.9) | 3 ms | 63 ms | 1.0 s | 0.15–0.42 s |
| `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0` | **2.3 s** | 15 ms | 60 ms | 1.06 s | 0.14 s |

A core edit (`std-avrac/src/core/side_table.av`) with the net on: 95.5 / 96.5 s, emit 0.45 s.
**The net costs about 96 s of every warm edit.** That is ~40x everything a backend could save, so it
comes first; it's outside this lane, and I'm reporting it, not touching it.

With the net off, the edit re-emits 1 module (1,895 fns, 83,001 instrs): built 0.10 s + codegen 0.55 s
= ~0.65 s LLVM. The rest of the 1.06 s "emit" row is driver work in `build.av`'s `linked` before
`clock.mark("emit")`: `homed`/`closed` over the whole program, an `object_of` store lookup for every
read file, and `objects_kept`. That driver part (~0.4 s) is not LLVM, and no backend change removes it.

## 3. Per kind of fn: cost follows instructions, about 5 µs each in LLVM, 1.3 µs in ours
From the 32 cold modules (modules with >1,000 fns):
- Codegen: **4.8–5.9 µs per IR instruction** across typical modules (34–56 instrs/fn), so 200–290 µs per fn.
- Our IR -> LLVM IR: **1.0–1.6 µs per instruction** (about 1/4 of codegen).
- Outliers: a branch-heavy module (116 instrs/fn) at 7.6 µs/instr, and a straight-line one
  (166 instrs/fn, mostly static data / long bodies) at 2.8 µs/instr. More blocks per instruction
  cost more (ISel + regalloc at -O0 scale with blocks and live ranges).
- Not split: object writing. `file_put` and the rename aren't clocked; the codegen figure ends with
  the object in a memory buffer.

## 4. A direct dev emitter (IR -> x86-64 / arm64 machine code, no LLVM)
**Savings, measured basis.** A single-pass template emitter typically runs at ~5–10x LLVM -O0's speed.
Taking it at 0.3–0.6 µs/instr, including building its own instruction stream:
- Warm one-edit (net off): 0.65 s -> ~0.05–0.10 s, **saving ~0.55–0.6 s of 2.3 s (~25%)**.
  The 0.4 s of driver work and 0.14 s of link stay.
- Cold: 11.1 s CPU -> ~1–2 s CPU, saving ~3–5 s wall on 4 cores, **~2–3% of 152 s**.
- Peak RSS: LLVM's module/context memory goes away; not measured separately.

**Cost to build (estimate).** It replaces 4,009 lines today (`backend/llvm*.av` 2,087 + `llvm_wrapper.c` 1,922).
- 36 `Ins` kinds, each lowered to a fixed template per ISA, plus the runtime calls' C ABI
  (SysV x86-64 and AAPCS64, narrow-int sign/zero extension as `rt_arg` does now).
- A register allocator good enough for dev builds: linear scan, or everything spilled to frame slots.
- **Unwinding is the hard part**: the IR has cleanup regions and landing pads (`unwinds`, `open`,
  `blocks` in `Emit`), so the emitter has to write `.eh_frame` CFI plus LSDA tables in the
  personality's format. That's the part LLVM gives for free today.
- Object files: ELF (Linux) and Mach-O (macOS arm64), with relocations for calls, globals and static
  boxes (`Ins.StaticAddr`, headered globals per runtime/avra_box.h).
- Optional DWARF line tables for debuggers.
- Rough size: 8–15k lines, plus a differential test (the evaluator vs the LLVM build vs the dev
  emitter over every `.expected` program), since the three engines must agree.

**Recommendation.**
1. Not now. The warm loop's first ~96 s is the net. After that, the 0.4 s driver part of "emit"
   (whole-program `closed`/`homed` per edit, a store lookup per file) is cheaper to fix than a
   backend, and of the same order as what a backend saves.
2. If the net goes away and per-edit cost becomes the target, a direct emitter buys ~0.55 s per edit.
   The cheaper middle path to measure first: keep LLVM but run codegen per fn and cache the object
   code by body key, so an edit re-codegens only the changed bodies rather than the whole module
   (today 1 edited file -> 1,895 fns re-emitted).

Raw outputs: /work/probes/devb-cold.out, /work/probes/devb-cold2.out (time -v), /work/probes/loop/*.out.
EOF

# The warm edit loop on main: make try (a leaf and a core edit), then one-edit check and build of packages/cli, 3 runs each.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
LEAF=packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av
CORE=packages/std-avrac/src/core/side_table.av
mkdir -p build/loop
cp $LEAF build/loop/leaf.orig
cp $CORE build/loop/core.orig
edit() { # edit <file> <orig-copy> <anchor> <stamp>: the original with the stamp inserted after the anchor
  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" <<'PY'
import sys
dest, orig, anchor, stamp = sys.argv[1:5]
text = open(orig, encoding="utf-8").read()
assert text.count(anchor) == 1, anchor
open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(anchor, anchor + " " + stamp, 1))
PY
}
# a cold build and check first, so the one-edit runs are warm
./avra build packages/cli > build/loop/cold.out 2>&1; echo "cold build exit $?"
./avra check packages/cli > build/loop/coldcheck.out 2>&1; echo "cold check exit $?"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  s=$(date +%s%N)
  edit $LEAF build/loop/leaf.orig "· memo" "t$i$(date +%s%N)"
  ./avra check --time packages/cli > build/loop/c$i.out 2> build/loop/c$i.err; st=$?
  e=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "check run $i exit $st ms $(( (e - s) / 1000000 )) $(grep -h -o 'held [0-9]*/[0-9]*' build/loop/c$i.err build/loop/c$i.out | head -n 1)"
  s=$(date +%s%N)
  ./avra build --time packages/cli > build/loop/b$i.out 2> build/loop/b$i.err; st=$?
  e=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "build run $i exit $st ms $(( (e - s) / 1000000 )) $(grep -h -o 'held [0-9]*/[0-9]*' build/loop/b$i.err build/loop/b$i.out | head -n 1)"
done
cp build/loop/leaf.orig $LEAF
for i in 1 2 3; do
  edit $LEAF build/loop/leaf.orig "· memo" "m$i$(date +%s%N)"
  s=$(date +%s%N); make try > build/loop/try_leaf$i.out 2>&1; st=$?; e=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "make try leaf run $i exit $st ms $(( (e - s) / 1000000 ))"
  cp build/loop/leaf.orig $LEAF
  edit $CORE build/loop/core.orig "holds [" "k$i$(date +%s%N)"
  s=$(date +%s%N); make try > build/loop/try_core$i.out 2>&1; st=$?; e=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "make try core run $i exit $st ms $(( (e - s) / 1000000 ))"
  cp build/loop/core.orig $CORE
done
cmp -s build/loop/leaf.orig $LEAF && cmp -s build/loop/core.orig $CORE && echo "restored both"

- Fix used: promote gen-1 (`build/avra-try`) to `build/avra`, then `make avra`.

# A REFUSAL MUST SPEAK: the build's own words went to /dev/null, so a compiler
# that refused its own source reported only "make: *** Error 2" and the next
# reader ran `./avra build packages/cli` by hand to find out why.
avra: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@mkdir -p build
	@# the log is BOUNDED: only its last 200 KB is ever read, and a build failing in a
	@# loop filled the volume twice (tools/capped.sh, which also carries the status).
	@# THE COMPILER IS THE OPTIMISED BUILD: `avra build` makes a dev binary, and every compiler a ladder
	@# climbs with reads this spelling, where only today's knows `--release`.
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-build.out 200000 env AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ./avra build packages/cli || { cat build/avra-build.out; exit 1; }
	@mkdir -p build
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra.next && mv -f build/avra.next build/avra
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@# what this binary was built from, for a worktree that wants to start from it
	@sh tools/work built-from . > build/.avra-built-from 2>/dev/null || rm -f build/.avra-built-from
	@sh tools/work deposit . || true
	@echo "avra: build/avra"

# WHAT A COMPILER BUILD LEAVES, one path a line: the binary, its hot leaves
# and every object it links with each object's stamp and dependency list.
# A cache of built compilers (tools/sprite-remote.sh) keeps exactly these.
compiler-files:
	@printf '%s\n' build/avra build/avra_hot.bc build/avra_hot.inc $(sort $(COMPILER_OBJS) \
	  $(patsubst %.o,%.sha,$(filter %.o,$(COMPILER_OBJS))) $(patsubst %.o,%.d,$(filter %.o,$(COMPILER_OBJS))))

# THE COMPILER FROM WHATEVER STANDS: the standing binary builds this tree
# GENS times (one `make avra` advances one generation; two reach a fixed point), and where none stands or
# it cannot read the tree — new syntax, a refusal about its own source — the
# seed bootstraps it, a FULL build, so a source wrong for real still dies.
# A SEED EMITTED FROM THIS VERY SOURCE comes first: linking it already is the
# compiler this tree builds (tools/seed_is_tree.sh), so no ladder and no
# standing compiler can do better, and a tree too new for every published one
# still builds; with rungs named, it is their product too.
# RUNGS are the tree's `Rung:` commits, oldest first (tools/rungs.sh): each is
# built by the product of the one before (tools/ladder.sh), starting from the
# standing compiler or the seed as linked, and HEAD by the last; a laddered
# tree never falls back to the seed, which cannot read a rung. The last rung's
# product stays at build/avra-ladder. LADDER_BASE is the base each rung is
# replayed on (tools/ladder.sh's AVRA_LADDER_BASE). GEN_BOUND bounds each build in seconds
# (tools/bounded.sh names the cause), LADDER_BOUND the whole ladder; STORE_ASIDE
# is where an older compiler's store goes before the bootstrap, since a store is
# one compiler's.
RUNGS ?=
LADDER_BASE ?=
GEN_BOUND ?=
LADDER_BOUND ?= 900
STORE_ASIDE ?=
GENS ?= 2
BOUNDED = $(if $(GEN_BOUND),sh tools/bounded.sh $(GEN_BOUND) )
compiler:
	@gens() { n=$(GENS); while [ "$$n" -gt 0 ]; do $(BOUNDED)$(MAKE) -s avra || return 1; n=$$((n - 1)); done; }; \
	if [ "$$(sh tools/seed_is_tree.sh "$$(sh tools/sources_hash.sh)" "$$(cat bootstrap/seed.sources 2>/dev/null)")" = seed ]; then \
	  echo "compiler: the committed seed was emitted from this tree — linked, not climbed"; \
	  $(BOUNDED)$(MAKE) -s bootstrap || exit 1; \
	  [ -z "$(strip $(RUNGS))" ] || cp build/avra build/avra-ladder; \
	elif [ -n "$(strip $(RUNGS))" ]; then \
	  [ -x build/avra ] || $(MAKE) -s recover || { echo "compiler: the ladder has no start — none stands and the seed did not link"; exit 1; }; \
	  product=$$(AVRA_LADDER_BASE=$(LADDER_BASE) AVRA_LADDER_S=$(LADDER_BOUND) sh tools/ladder.sh build/avra $(RUNGS)) \
	    || { echo "compiler: the ladder failed — a rung did not build with the compiler of the rung before it"; exit 1; }; \
	  cp "$$product" build/avra-ladder && cp "$$product" build/avra.next && mv -f build/avra.next build/avra; \
	  sh tools/ladder.sh --clean "$${AVRA_LADDER_DIR:-$${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/ladder}"; \
	  gens || { echo "compiler: the ladder's product did not build this tree — no seed can read a rung"; exit 1; }; \
	elif [ -x build/avra ] && gens; then :; else \
	  if [ -n "$(STORE_ASIDE)" ] && [ -d .avra-cache ]; then mv .avra-cache "$(STORE_ASIDE)"; fi; \
	  echo "compiler: the standing compiler did not build this tree — bootstrapping from the seed"; \
	  $(BOUNDED)$(MAKE) -s bootstrap; \
	fi

# THE EDIT LOOP: the source built by the STANDING compiler into
# build/avra-try, never over it — so the builder's print, and every row its
# store holds, stands from one edit to the next. `./avra-try` runs it. A
# change the compiler must READ to build itself (codegen, the front end, a
# refusal about its own source) reaches the product only through `make avra`.
try: $(COMPILER_OBJS)
	@sh tools/capped.sh build/avra-try-build.out 200000 env AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release ./avra build packages/cli --time || { cat build/avra-try-build.out; exit 1; }
	@grep '^time: ast' build/avra-try-build.out | grep -oE 'held [0-9]+/[0-9]+' || true
	@cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra-try.next && mv -f build/avra-try.next build/avra-try
	@codesign -f -s - build/avra-try 2>/dev/null || true
	@rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
	@echo "try: build/avra-try — ./avra-try runs it"

# THE WARM EDIT LOOP, measured: a one-edit check and build of the cli, and `make try` on a leaf and a core edit.
edit-loop:
	@sh tools/db_measure/edit_loop.sh

# THE INSTALL: the binary under bin/, and what it finds from its own
# directory — the runtime's object and every std package — under
# lib/avra/. A program anywhere then says `use @std.io` with no
# manifest row, and links.
PREFIX ?= /usr/local
install: avra
	@mkdir -p $(PREFIX)/bin $(PREFIX)/lib/avra/std

    saved answers: a record and a list read in place hold only numbers, their bytes handed beside them
    
    A SavedRecord and a SavedList held their SavedSource, so each was a box
    made per node read: 35.7 M a cold build. They hold only where they start
    and their counts now, and travel in registers; every SavedSlots read takes
    the source beside the node. record_in/list_in read a child that must be
    there without a nullable. Octets copy straight out of the source. The
    Saved derive's readers take the source as SOURCE_NAME, and each query has
    one answer_read door binding its answer's source; a door answering a node
    in place answers it beside its source (SavedAt), and SavedBytes.root_at
    makes one. The engine's in-place holders (a mapped pack, a frontier's
    columns, a tape's sections, a record's laid words) hold their source once.

    makes one. The engine's in-place holders (a mapped pack, a frontier's

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
# A test row runs every suite (AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1), so it names every failing case, never only the first.
#
# GATE_OLD_PATH=0 drops every row that compares against the old path (they read AVRA_PROGRAM=0);
# when the old path goes, its default goes to 0 and those rows go with one line each.
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root" || exit 1
unset AVRA_PROGRAM AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE
export AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1
# THE NET IS OFF unless a row's claim is the net: the old path's check before every program-layer
# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0

OLD_PATH=${GATE_OLD_PATH:-1}
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
ROW_SECS=${GATE_ROW_SECS:-2400}
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
60:fmt        fmt --check on every .av the diff from <base> changes (tools/fmt_changed.sh); <base> is the program landed last, never a batch's own base
341:fmt_on() {
343:    row fmt-changed env AVRA=build/avra sh tools/fmt_changed.sh "$1" HEAD
439:        fmt) fmt_on "${1:-}" ;;

fixes the lead sends. Lane brief rules: no `rm` (use `find ... -delete`), no `git stash`, no

`build/avra-try fmt --write` on touched .av files before committing, ONE heavy build at a time, don't end a
turn while a job runs, post to the lead only at a bundle/blocker/ruling (at most 12 lines).

# Avra — clean-room compiler

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

the body exists, answer:

   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`

only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted

  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.

  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY

  standard signature and is not a verb.

  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph

  caller's bytes outlive the statement, and is keepable only because
  the caller's own box goes straight through; migrating the WALL seat

  call `.bytes()` — minting a box whose only holder is that call,
  dead at return, handing C a dangling pointer every time with the
  caller having done nothing wrong. The face takes the new type too,

  contract always required. THE SEATS WHERE THIS BITES ARE FEW AND

  second-generation product traps, run the first generation over the
  same source before reading the trap as the tree's.

  (then spelled `explain @name` and `explain process`) rooted at "."
  analysed nothing from the day they landed,
  and read as "no fn declared in this package" for a fn declared
  right there. The caller's directory is `AVRA_CWD`, exported by the
  shim before it moves; a command that reads the package it stands in

  relative one read where the tree stands found nothing from another
  directory, and read from a package's own root it walked past the
